items.title: Siemens and AGIBOT design humanoid grippers from text prompts
items.summary: Siemens and AGIBOT developed an AI agent workflow to design humanoid robot grippers from text prompts. The agent uses a written task description to select a gripper, modify its geometry in Designcenter, and perform virtual simulations. This process coordinates engineering software functions through MCP integration to adapt the design to the user's handling requirements. This method aims to simplify complex engineering workflows by focusing on the required handling, not individual printing steps. Siemens intends to further this work with an adaptive production cell integrating additive manufacturing and automation.
items.audio_script: From Humanoid.guide, "Siemens and AGIBOT design humanoid grippers from text prompts". This report details an AI agent workflow developed by Siemens and AGIBOT for designing humanoid robot grippers based on text prompts, demonstrating a method for streamlining complex engineering workflows. The process involves an AI agent that uses a written task description to select a gripper, modify its geometry within Designcenter, and execute virtual simulations. This system coordinates various engineering software functions through MCP integration to adapt the design according to specified handling requirements. The methodology prioritizes the required handling specification over individual printing steps, aiming to simplify the engineering process significantly. Siemens plans to expand this work by integrating additive manufacturing and automation into an adaptive production cell. This development indicates a step toward more intuitive, prompt-based design for advanced robotics systems.

items.title: China issues five humanoid robot standards covering testing
items.summary: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology issued five humanoid robot standards on November 16, 2026, to address inconsistencies in capability claims, equipment interfaces, and data management. These standards cover capability assessment, training facilities, training data, integrated electric drive joints, and dexterous hands. A capability classification standard uses six levels (L0 to L5) across four dimensions to provide a detailed profile for development and comparison. Additional standards specify requirements for training sites, hardware, data lifecycle, and safety protocols. The goal is to facilitate the comparison and integration of humanoid robots by standardizing various aspects of their development.

These standards encompass capability assessment, training facilities, training data, integrated electric drive joints, and dexterous hands. A capability classification standard utilizes six levels, L0 to L5, across four dimensions to establish a detailed profile for development and comparison. Further standards delineate requirements for training sites, hardware specifications, data lifecycle management, and safety protocols. This standardization aims to facilitate the comparison and integration of humanoid robots through standardized development parameters. The establishment of these benchmarks sets a framework for industry-wide development and interoperability in humanoid robotics.

items.title: Medtronic’s Hugo surgical robot ready for bigger operation
items.summary: The Hugo surgical robot has received FDA clearance for general surgery procedures in the U.S., covering abdominal and lower abdominal operations. This modular system allows surgeons to use only necessary robotic arms, offering flexibility in multi-quadrant procedures. Medtronic is integrating Artificial Intelligence into the Hugo platform to provide real-time intraoperative guidance and optimize patient outcomes. Robotic surgery enhances surgeon experience by reducing physical strain and improving visualization through 3D imaging and intuitive controls. Medtronic is prioritizing cost, training, and support to increase the accessibility of robotic surgery globally.

items.title: Watco expands Intramotev autonomous railcar operations to Texas
items.summary: Intramotev has agreed with Watco to deploy its TugVolt autonomous railcar technology to a second site in Seadrift, Texas. This expansion builds upon prior work completed at Watco's terminal in Wood River, Illinois. Intramotev will use TugVolt units to switch railcars within an industrial facility in Seadrift. The technology has already been used at Watco's Wood River site for moving soda ash. Intramotev is the first company to commercially deploy autonomous freight railcars globally.

Intramotev will utilize TugVolt units to manage the switching of railcars within an industrial facility in Seadrift. This technology has previously been successfully employed at the Watco Wood River site for the movement of soda ash. Intramotev holds the distinction of being the first company globally to commercially deploy autonomous freight railcars. This expansion signifies further real-world application of autonomous logistics systems in heavy industrial settings. Future developments in autonomous freight movement are anticipated to follow this operational extension.

items.title: MassRobotics launching marine robotics facility on Boston Harbor
items.summary: MassRobotics is developing a marine robotics facility at the Boston Fish Pier to allow startups to build, launch, and test robots in Boston Harbor. Construction is being done in partnership with the Massachusetts Port Authority (Massport), with plans for the facility to open in early 2028. The facility will feature testing equipment, including a water tank and launch gear, to simplify access to water testing for marine robotics companies. This setup aims to accelerate innovation by creating a direct loop between building prototypes and testing them in the harbor. MassRobotics currently supports over 100 global startups by providing this integrated testing environment.

items.title: How to prototype robot control logic before committing to industrial hardware
items.summary: Prototype robot control logic on a microcontroller first to sketch sequences, timing, and I/O behavior before committing to expensive industrial hardware. Testing on constrained boards reveals timing assumptions and potential failures that are often missed during hardware commissioning. Prototyping allows teams to deliberately test state transitions and handle edge cases that are impractical on live systems. While a prototype proves sequence logic, it does not account for crucial aspects like safety ratings, EMC performance, or fieldbus determinism. The prototype serves as a specification, guiding the design of the final, safety-rated industrial system.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "How to prototype robot control logic before committing to industrial hardware". This report details the process of prototyping robot control logic on a microcontroller to sketch sequences and timing before committing to industrial hardware, revealing that testing on constrained boards exposes timing assumptions and potential failures often overlooked during hardware commissioning. Teams utilizing this method can deliberately test state transitions and handle edge cases that are impractical on live systems, establishing a specification that guides the design of final, safety-rated industrial systems, although prototypes do not account for safety ratings or fieldbus determinism. This approach mandates a foundational logic test prior to physical implementation across the automation sector.

items.title: ‘The doom of humanity’: will the quest to make robotic hands render us obsolete?
items.summary: Replicating the dexterity of human hands is a major challenge for robotics, as the ability to feedback and feed forward sensory information is inherently complex. Human hands evolved through a combination of cognitive power and physical dexterity, involving intricate sensory feedback and predictive modeling. While humanoid robots are being developed, achieving the necessary dexterity for real-world tasks remains difficult, leading to a race in developing advanced robotic hands. Companies are focusing on specialized dexterous hands for specific tasks, with significant investment in this area globally. Ultimately, the future impact on jobs depends on how quickly artificial dexterity can be replicated in machines.
items.audio_script: From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "‘The doom of humanity’: will the quest to make robotic hands render us obsolete?" reports on the challenges in replicating human hand dexterity through robotics and the resulting focus on advanced robotic hand development. The ability to replicate the dexterity of human hands presents a significant challenge for robotics because achieving this requires complex sensory feedback and predictive modeling, which evolved through a combination of cognitive power and physical dexterity. Research is currently focused on developing specialized dexterous hands for specific tasks, with substantial global investment directed towards this area. The pace at which artificial dexterity can be replicated in machines will determine the ultimate impact on labor markets. The technology sector should monitor advancements in fine motor control systems for future developments.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: ROS 2 Jazzy for macOS (Apple Silicon): release 26.11.20.9, self-contained, Gazebo included, Nav2 up in 78 s
items.summary: A self-contained ROS 2 Jazzy package is now available for macOS Apple Silicon via Homebrew, including Gazebo. This build features a significantly faster startup time, reducing a TurtleBot 4 with Nav2 simulation from several minutes to 78 seconds. The package bundles necessary libraries, making it resilient to Homebrew updates. It includes key navigation and simulation tools like Nav2, MoveIt 2, and various middleware. The project emphasizes upstream contributions, aiming to track official ROS 2 development rather than creating a full fork.

The development focused on creating a build that is self-contained and resilient to Homebrew updates by bundling necessary libraries. This specific package achieves a significant improvement in simulation startup time, reducing the time required for a TurtleBot 4 with Nav2 simulation to 78 seconds. The package integrates essential tools such as Nav2, MoveIt 2, and various middleware, emphasizing tracking official ROS 2 development. This release establishes a streamlined environment for robotics simulation on Apple Silicon platforms. Further developments in cross-platform ROS tooling are anticipated.

items.title: Ep#118: Devol Robotics
items.summary: Devol Robotics develops physics-grounded foundation models to enable precise robotic manipulation by incorporating understanding of force and contact. They use an Interaction World Model (IWM) to learn visual-geometric representations that predict stiffness and damping, based on interaction geometry. The Devol-ONE model unifies vision-language understanding, world prediction, and action generation within a single autoregressive framework. This approach allows robots to reliably complete complex, compliant tasks by predicting physical dynamics during action planning. Experiments showed that incorporating physical priors significantly improved success rates and efficiency in contact-rich assembly tasks.
